final3.name: KeyPouch amenity dispenser + keyed refill pouch
final3.case_for: Only candidate with a real consumable lock-in and recurring revenue. Hardware at EUR 35 vs ~EUR 10-13 landed, refill at EUR 2-6/L contribution; the shared analysis puts year-1 per-account contribution after CAC at roughly EUR 140-960 (base ~440-570), all ASSUMPTION. Cheap IP (~EUR 1-1.5k). Validation sprint is cheap (EUR 400-800) and gives a clear go/no-go.
final3.moat: Account-level consumable lock-in via keyed cap/pouch fitment, plus EU registered design (EUR 350), Danish utility model (~EUR 320), optional EU TM. Chair view: the legal moat is thin (key interface likely excluded as must-fit/technical function; no Swedish utility model; design-around plausible in 1-3 months per red team vs 6-12 per analysis). The durable part is installed base, distributor/OEM partnership and service, not geometry. Defensibility cut from 3 to 2.
final3.key_risks: (1) Buyers reject EUR 8-12/L vs generic EUR 3-5/L bulk (unverified) and lock-in itself. (2) Meadow KAPSUL, Tork/Essity, Katrin etc. already run cartridge lock-in and janitorial distribution. (3) PPWR hotel-minis timing (probably 2030, not verified) gives no 2027 urgency and favours any refill system. (4) Founder channel fit is weak: VELUX and Nilfisk contacts are not hotel amenity buyers (Nilfisk janitorial distributors are the best lever). (5) Capital EUR 11-14k exceeds the cap; SOM of 25-45 accounts is not credible at 10 h/week (red team says EUR 3-12k revenue). (6) Cosmetics Regulation compliance and filler MOQs if pouches carry product; multiple SKUs.
final3.must_validate_before_sourcing: Gate before any tooling or first order: 5 prepaid pilots or 10 LOIs at >= EUR 7/L, ideally 1-2 janitorial distributors (ex-Nilfisk) willing to carry it; IP attorney opinion on the key interface plus freedom-to-operate vs Meadow/Tork; two filler quotes with MOQ; test with off-the-shelf dispenser + 3D-printed keyed cap and a single hand-soap SKU; fetch current sources on PPWR hotel-minis date and Meadow pricing (not verified this run). Cap capital under ~EUR 5k by using off-the-shelf dispenser bodies; kill if buyers will not pay > EUR 6/L.

final3.name: Nordic FTX Filter Club
final3.case_for: Best recurring-revenue structure with a B2B channel (installers) and ~50% margin on EUR 24-39 sets; cheap to test with no stock and no lab fee. Highest probability of producing a real, if modest, side-business. It does NOT meet the moat bar as submitted.
final3.moat: As submitted: none that qualifies. ISO 16890 report and RISE P-mark are purchasable by any competitor; frame design must fit OEM housings so registered design is narrow; installer relationships are non-exclusive; subscription has no lock-in under EU cancellation rules. Both red teams agree (defensibility 1). It qualifies for a 2 only if converted into a contract moat: an exclusive/preferred-supplier deal with one OEM or a multi-year filter-service agreement with a housing portfolio or service chain.
final3.key_risks: (1) Compatible filters probably already sold in SE/DK; certified premium may be small. (2) OEM warranty messaging (Genvex says only originals keep performance) and trade terms. (3) Founders' ex-VELUX network reaches roofers/window installers, not ventilation service firms; 8-15 installers in year 1 is optimistic (3-5 more plausible). (4) Lab cost unquoted and may be EUR 6-15k across SKUs. (5) Year-1 contribution EUR 5-12k may not repay EUR 7-10k outlay; D2C first order is break-even to negative after CAC. (6) Seasonality: first revenue spring 2027. (7) Market sizing entirely assumption-led.
final3.must_validate_before_sourcing: Zero-spend gates: sourced scan of existing compatible FTX filters and prices in SE/DK; written lab quotes (RISE + one other) with kill above EUR 5k all-in; at least 5 written trial commitments from ventilation service firms (not roofers) at EUR 24 trade; ideally one OEM or service-chain exclusivity LOI; waitlist test (25 sign-ups or 10 pre-orders under EUR 10 each). Note: the dollar-light test costs ~EUR 300-450. Without an exclusivity element, treat as a small reseller business, not a brand.

final3.name: Exclusive-artist wooden jigsaw puzzle
final3.case_for: Lowest capital risk of the licence plays: no tooling (laser cut), a EUR 1-2.5k recoupable advance, and a pre-sale gate (under EUR 500) that proves or kills demand before the EUR 6-7k order. Price EUR 79 gives ~EUR 24 contribution; organic artist-audience orders reach +EUR 16-24 per unit. Design-led founders can execute it. It is a consumer art product, so it diversifies the shortlist, but it is weaker on moat and repeat than the top two.
final3.moat: Exclusive artist licence for the puzzle category (target 5+ years, Nordic/EU, first right on new works) plus numbered editions. Chair view: a contract moat that blocks only one artist, not the category; a competitor signs another illustrator in weeks and the artist can leave at term. Real only to the extent the artist is a proven EUR 60+ seller with an audience that brings its own traffic. Defensibility 2, not 3.
final3.key_risks: (1) Artist audience may buy EUR 20-40 prints, not a EUR 79 puzzle; paid CAC EUR 25-45 exceeds ~EUR 24 contribution. (2) Artist holds all leverage at renewal. (3) No repeat revenue. (4) Q4 2026 is gone: first real gift season Q4 2027, so cash and risk are tied up ~13 months unless pre-sales justify a spring launch. (5) Post-2020 puzzle trend may have normalised; Wentworth/Liberty-type premium makers already exist (unverified). (6) B2B/museum-shop channel is not a founder edge. (7) Shipping/returns costs likely understated (EUR 10-14 vs 8).
final3.must_validate_before_sourcing: Signed LOI with a named artist (100k+ followers, proven EUR 60+ product sales) with category exclusivity and artist co-marketing commitments; render-based Shopify pre-order page plus ~EUR 300 ads and 2 artist posts: pass at >= 60-80 paid pre-orders (or 150 refundable deposits) at under EUR 20 blended acquisition cost; EUR 150-300 laser-cut sample for quality; carrier quotes for fragile 1 kg SE/DK shipping; verify SE/DK packaging EPR and timber due diligence costs. Commit the EUR 8-10k only after the gate.

reserve.name: Estate-licensed reissue of small Nordic mid-century object
reserve.reason: Same licence logic as N035 with a slightly more durable asset (copyright-based exclusivity on a specific object, higher price anchor possible) but longer lead time (3-6 months to sign), adverse selection (good estates already tied to Rosendahl/Stelton/Artek), tooling EUR 1.5-3k and capital at the EUR 10k ceiling; activate only if a named estate gives indicative terms at advance <= EUR 1-2k, or if N035's artist gate fails.

cuts.name: BRF Ventilation Year-Pack
cuts.reason: Access-only moat (defensibility 1), buyer/payer mismatch (residents often own filter task), ~3x premium over a EUR 7-10 retail 3-pack, and one selling window a year; at best a service idea to fold into N014 interviews.

cuts.name: Nordic Light-Seal Kit
cuts.reason: No moat above 1, paid CAC exceeds ~EUR 15 contribution, no repeat, B2B needs ~150 accounts (more hours than the founders have), and DIY strips at EUR 3-10 plus VELUX redesign risk.

vs_first_run: Marginally better, not decisively. Structurally improved: two of the three (N020, N014) have recurring revenue and B2B channels, N020 has an actual lock-in mechanism, and prices are EUR 35-79 rather than EUR 15-25, so contribution can absorb some CAC. But defensibility after red-team is only 2, 1 and 2 versus the first run's 1-2, so the moat gain is one notch at best and N014 is no better than the Trickle-vent refresh kit it resembles. The licence plays (N035, N034) replace a copyable look with a contract that only blocks one artist and expires. Every number is an ASSUMPTION; both analysts and red teams had no live web evidence (search budget exhausted, hosts blocked, Firecrawl out of credits) and I could not re-verify here, so nothing in this chair's ranking is source-backed beyond the retail prices and SCB figure already cited.
honest_overall_assessment: None of these is a genuinely good idea for EUR 5-10k as it stands. The best (KeyPouch) is a plausible but unproven niche B2B play whose lock-in is legally thin, whose true capital is EUR 11-14k and whose buyers are not in the founders' networks; it is worth a EUR 400-800 test, not a EUR 10k bet. The filter idea is the most likely to make some money and the least likely to be defensible. The licence ideas are gated pre-sale experiments, not moats. Honest recommendation: run the cheap kill tests on N020 and N014 in parallel (about 6 weeks, under EUR 1.3k combined), run N035's pre-sale only if an artist engages, and be prepared to conclude that no candidate clears the bar. The funnel has not yet produced the thing the founders' edges point to: a product sold through building-industry channels (VELUX/installer/housing association relationships) with a patentable or certified mechanism or consumable. If all gates fail, the next screen should start from that edge rather than from consumer categories.
